model.name: ADSS
model.definition: What the business means by the things it records.
model.description: One model for the whole platform. Entities arrive as the questions that need them arrive, and a new attribute, entity or relationship is always a new structure rather than a change to one something already depends on.

entities.name: ORDER
entities.definition: A commitment by the business to supply goods, created when it accepts a customer's request for them.
entities.description: One order is one such commitment. It begins on the day the business accepts it and is settled by delivering what was promised, to where it was promised.

attributes.name: ORDER_NUMBER
attributes.definition: The number the business uses when it refers to one particular order.
attributes.description: Unique across all orders, and never reused once issued.

attributes.name: PLACED_ON
attributes.definition: The day the business accepted the order, and from which the order exists.
attributes.description: An order is placed once. This is the date every question about when demand occurred is measured against.

attributes.name: DESTINATION_COUNTRY
attributes.definition: The country the business has undertaken to deliver the order to.
attributes.description: Where the goods are going, which is not necessarily where the customer is. A question about demand by geography means this unless it says otherwise.

attributes.name: ORDER_DESTINATION_COUNTRY_EFF_TMSTP
attributes.description: Automatically generated timestamp tracking last change
